summary: Annual financial return filed with Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario. Total direct written premiums for Ontario operations: $2.1B across personal and commercial lines. Combined ratio of 94.2% reflects strong underwriting discipline. Investment income of $185M supports overall profitability. Capital adequacy ratio (MCT) at 235% — well above OSFI minimum of 150%. No material adverse findings from actuarial review. Appointed actuary opinion: reserves adequate with margin.

Quarterly IFRS 17 compliance filing. Insurance contract liabilities measured under General Measurement Model for all commercial lines and Premium Allocation Approach for personal auto and property. Risk adjustment calculated at 8.5% confidence level using cost-of-capital approach. Contractual service margin release pattern reflects expected claims emergence. Key change this quarter: updated loss development factors for commercial auto reflecting improved large loss experience. Discount rates updated to reflect Q4 2023 yield curve movements.

Semi-annual Minimum Capital Test (MCT) filing. Total capital available: $4.2B. Total capital required: $1.8B. MCT ratio: 233%. Tier 1 capital ratio: 198%. Capital composition: common equity 72%, retained earnings 18%, subordinated debt 10%. Stress testing results: under 1-in-200 year catastrophe scenario, MCT would remain above 180%. No capital actions required. Board risk appetite maintained at 200% minimum MCT.

Annual catastrophe exposure filing per OSFI Guideline B-9. Key exposures: Toronto earthquake (250-year PML: $380M), Ontario windstorm ($290M), Alberta wildfire ($210M). Reinsurance program provides coverage to 1-in-500 year event level. Net retained exposure after reinsurance: $75M first event, $50M subsequent events. Aggregate excess program in place for frequency protection. Cat model validation completed using AIR and RMS — results within 10% of each other. Exposure concentration in GTA continues to be primary accumulation risk.

FSRA market conduct examination response. Examination covered claims handling practices for personal auto bodily injury claims (AB) for the period 2022-2023. Findings: 1) 94% of BI claims acknowledged within 5-day regulatory requirement, 2) 88% of treatment plans approved within 10 business days, 3) IE (Independent Examination) requests made within regulatory guidelines in 97% of cases, 4) Two areas for improvement identified: a) catastrophic impairment determination timeliness (78% vs 85% target), b) disclosure of IE report copies to claimants within required timeframe (82% compliance). Corrective action plan submitted and approved by FSRA.

Annual compliance report filed with FINTRAC. Reporting obligations met: 142 large cash transaction reports filed, 23 suspicious transaction reports (STRs) submitted, 0 terrorist property reports. Enhanced due diligence applied to 34 commercial accounts per risk-based approach. Staff training completion rate: 98% (target 95%). Internal audit of AML program completed Q1 2024 — no material deficiencies. Program effectiveness assessment: compliant with PCMLTFA requirements. Key risk area: premium financing arrangements — additional monitoring implemented.

Mandatory privacy breach report following cyber incident at Maple Tech Solutions (insured commercial client). Breach involved potential exposure of policyholder data through client's compromised systems. Our data affected: 342 policyholders' names, policy numbers, and coverage details were in client's records as Certificate of Insurance data. No financial information (bank accounts, credit cards) or sensitive personal information (SIN, health) exposed. Notification letters sent to all 342 affected individuals within 72 hours. Credit monitoring offered for 12 months. Root cause: client's failure to maintain security standards per our vendor data sharing agreement.

Annual ORSA filed with OSFI per Guideline E-19. Key risks assessed: 1) Insurance risk — loss ratio volatility modelled at +/- 5 points (within risk appetite), 2) Market risk — interest rate sensitivity (100bps parallel shift = $45M impact), 3) Credit risk — reinsurer counterparty exposure concentrated in top 5 (all rated A+ or above), 4) Operational risk — cyber risk rated as 'elevated' with mitigation program underway, 5) Climate risk — physical risk exposure to flood and wildfire increasing 3-5% annually, transition risk limited given liability portfolio composition. Board approved risk appetite statement reaffirmed.

Annual reinsurance filing per OSFI Guideline B-3. Program structure: Property cat XL ($500M limit xs $75M retention), Casualty XL ($50M limit xs $10M retention), Property per-risk XL ($25M limit xs $5M retention), Motor XL ($10M limit xs $2M retention). Lead reinsurers: Swiss Re (25%), Munich Re (20%), Lloyd's (15%), SCOR (10%), others (30%). All reinsurers rated A- or above by AM Best. Credit risk charge under MCT: $12M. Collateral held for non-registered reinsurers: $45M in trust. No disputes outstanding from prior years.

TCFD-aligned climate risk disclosure per OSFI Guideline B-15. Physical risks: portfolio exposure to flood ($1.2B insured values in 100-year flood zones), wildfire ($680M in wildfire-prone areas), convective storm ($3.1B in hail corridors). Transition risks: limited given P&C portfolio — no fossil fuel exclusions but monitoring ESG scores of large commercial accounts. Strategy: implementing climate-adjusted pricing for high-risk zones starting Q1 2025, investing $15M in flood mitigation partnerships, requiring building code upgrades for commercial renewals in high-risk areas. Metrics: Scope 1+2 emissions reduced 12% year-over-year.

Appointed Actuary's annual report on policy liabilities per CIA Standards of Practice. Total net policy liabilities: $8.4B (gross: $9.2B net of reinsurance recoverable: $0.8B). Key assumptions: loss development factors based on 10-year triangles weighted toward recent experience, discount rates per IFRS 17 requirements, PFAD (Provision for Adverse Deviation) factors at CIA-prescribed minimums given mature book stability. Areas of uncertainty: 1) Long-tail casualty reserves for historical environmental and abuse claims, 2) Auto reform impact on Ontario BI development, 3) Inflation assumptions for property replacement costs. Opinion: liabilities are adequate to meet future obligations.

Annual conduct risk self-assessment per FSRA Fair Treatment of Customers framework. Categories assessed: product design (Low risk), distribution practices (Low risk), claims handling (Medium risk — improvement plan in place for BI timeliness), complaint resolution (Low risk), vulnerable customers (Medium risk — enhanced protocols being implemented for senior clients and those affected by catastrophic events). Ombudsman statistics: 45 complaints escalated in 12 months (down from 62 prior year), 38 resolved in insurer's favour, 4 resulted in additional payments, 3 pending. Overall assessment: satisfactory conduct risk profile with two areas of active improvement.

Quarterly investment portfolio compliance report. Total investment portfolio: $12.8B. Asset allocation: fixed income 68%, equities 18%, real estate 8%, alternatives 6%. Duration matching: asset duration 4.2 years vs liability duration 3.8 years (within +/- 0.5 year guideline). Credit quality: 92% investment grade (BBB- or above), 8% below investment grade (within 10% limit). Single issuer concentration: largest single corporate exposure 1.8% (within 3% limit). Stress test: 300bps rate rise = -$850M market value impact, offset by $620M liability decrease. Net interest rate risk: -$230M (within $300M board limit).

Annual insurance fraud activity report to Insurance Bureau of Canada. Total investigations opened: 89 (up 15% from prior year). Investigations by type: staged accidents 28%, exaggerated claims 22%, application fraud 18%, arson/intentional damage 12%, identity fraud 10%, other 10%. Claims denied for fraud: 34 (total value: $1.8M). Criminal referrals: 8. Successful prosecutions from prior year referrals: 3. Fraud savings (avoided payouts): $4.2M. Key trends: increase in organized tow truck fraud rings in GTA, emerging cyber-related fraud patterns, continued growth in application fraud using synthetic identities.

Earthquake exposure filing per OSFI requirements. Key zone exposures: Toronto/Hamilton (highest concentration — $2.1B total insured values within Modified Mercalli Intensity VII+ zone), Ottawa ($450M), Montreal operations ($380M via national accounts). Modelled losses (500-year return period): Toronto M6.0 scenario = gross $380M, net after reinsurance = $42M. Deductible assumptions: residential 5% of coverage, commercial 10% of coverage. Capacity adequacy: current reinsurance program provides coverage to modelled 1-in-750 year event. Concentration risk management: GTA portfolio capped at $2.5B total insured values per postal code forward sortation area.

Rate filing submitted to FSRA for personal auto insurance. Requesting overall average rate change of +3.8% effective October 1, 2024. Rate changes by coverage: Third Party Liability +2.1%, Accident Benefits +5.4%, Collision +4.2%, Comprehensive +1.8%. Justification: increased repair costs (parts inflation 8.2%), rising AB costs (treatment costs up 6.1%), improved loss experience in liability (partially offsetting). Impact on policyholders: 65% will see increase of less than $50/year, 20% will see decrease, 15% will see increase of $50-$100/year. Filing includes updated territory definitions reflecting claims patterns in GTA growth areas.

Annual pension plan compliance filing for defined benefit plan. Plan membership: 4,200 active members, 2,800 deferred vested, 3,100 pensioners. Funded status: 104% on going-concern basis, 92% on solvency basis. Solvency deficit: $85M. Minimum required contribution: $12M annually. Actual employer contribution: $18M (above minimum to improve solvency position). Investment return for year: 7.2% (above 6.0% discount rate assumption). Key risk: interest rate sensitivity — 100bps decrease in rates would reduce funded status by approximately 8 percentage points.

Annual technology and cybersecurity self-assessment per OSFI Guideline B-13. Key metrics: Mean time to detect incidents: 4.2 hours (target: <6 hours), Mean time to respond: 1.8 hours (target: <2 hours), Phishing simulation failure rate: 3.2% (target: <5%), Patch management: 99.1% critical patches applied within 72 hours, Penetration testing: annual external test completed with 2 medium findings (both remediated), Vendor risk assessments: 100% of critical vendors assessed annually. Areas of improvement: 1) Legacy application retirement (3 systems pending migration), 2) Third-party API security (new scanning tools deployed Q3). Overall maturity rating: Level 4 of 5 (target maintained).

Semi-annual complaint handling report per FSRA requirements. Total complaints received: 1,247 (personal auto: 52%, property: 28%, commercial: 12%, other: 8%). Resolution: 89% resolved within 30-day target, 96% within 60 days. Escalations to OmbudService: 22 (down from 31 same period prior year). Themes: auto claims repair quality disputes (18%), property claims scope disagreements (15%), renewal premium increases (14%), auto AB treatment plan delays (12%), subrogation deductible recovery timing (8%). Systemic issues identified: repair quality concerns led to vendor performance review program — 3 vendors removed from preferred list.

Group life and health insurance portfolio compliance filing. Total group lives insured: 285,000 across 450 employer groups. Key metrics: mortality experience 88% of expected (favourable), disability incidence trending upward (5% above expected — monitoring), drug cost trend: 7.8% increase year-over-year (driven by biologics and specialty drugs). Reserve adequacy: IBNR reserves at 102% of actuarial central estimate. Large claim pooling: 12 claims above $500,000 individual pooling point. Reinsurance adequacy: confirmed coverage to $5M per life. No concerns raised by OSFI in preliminary review.
